record_notes.DCP-LETT-1487: September 8 with supplied 1852 year acknowledges a missing Waterhouse note about holidays and Bravard fossil collecting. Darwin knows no certain current Buenos Aires contact, suggests several fossil localities and boat travel, and treats the old Rosas export restriction as uncertain. Offering his South America volume does not establish dispatch. Ray Society distribution delay is distinct from advance copies already received; no spare copy is available to give Waterhouse. The hoped visit and requested reading of Scalpellum/Ibla sexes are prospective. Old museum correspondence does not provide this prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-944: January 18 with supplied 1853 year, despite the low catalogue ID. Thanks for Waterhouse and Deshayes concern/advice but discourages foreign travel; recent bad fortnight is distinguished from improvement over preceding years. Wishes for Waterhouse original work do not assert a new publication. Clinical diary and Mammalia publication history in footnotes are separate apparatus. Missing Waterhouse note, not old 1845 insect or 1846 fossil inventory correspondence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1583: August 29, 1854 returns Indus fossil Balani and sends a separate group of acquired specimens, some named by Bosquet. The list is part of P2 after the signature; preserve genus continuations, variant labels and Bosquet attribution, not an undifferentiated prose sentence. Woodward is the museum specialist who should oversee mounting; Searles Valentine Wood is the donor of English fossil Balani. Few English specimens sent because Wood gives his collection. Dispatch/return language does not establish museum receipt or Darwin determination of every listed name. No incoming prompt identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1598: November 11, 1854 incoming incomplete letter supplies aberrant weevil genera after a missing Darwin request and catalogue loan. Read the entire two-column list, continuation blocks and P10–20 discussion. Curly-bracket species counts, totals and corrections are Darwin later pencil annotations, not Waterhouse original list. Waterhouse admits a theoretical preference against tiny families despite his initial no-theory claim. He contrasts natural groups with single-character classification, discusses Brachycerus, Byrsops, Hipporhinus/Leptops and Australian Amycteridae, and cautions that sound distribution generalisations require sound classification. Unknown genera remain explicitly unknown. The separate-sheet warning not to read is historical prose, not an agent instruction. Diagram independently viewed; source label placement retained. Later Darwin notes and 1858 publication are not November 11 availability to Darwin.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1625: Waterhouse memorandum dated after March 2, 1855 from a Wollaston exchange, with raw year-end bound; no exact March day chosen. Full list covers tarsal counts and sex differences in Anisotomidae, Cryptophagidae, Mycetophagidae and Staphylinidae, with continuations and ditto marks tied to their correct rows. Male/female symbols and counts are substantive. Raw diag/ramme debris and flattened layout are retained in the source projection. Darwin separate note, later chapter label and Origin quotations must not inherit the memorandum date or Waterhouse voice. The bibliographic entry under Wollaston does not itself authenticate the relevant letter or book. This tarsal list is not the missing atlas text discussed in 1641.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1641: March 4, 1855 follows a missing Waterhouse note claiming the atlas text should be present. Darwin has searched each page, insists the text is absent from the parcel, and distinguishes maps currently studied from maps and text previously seen at the Athenaeum. A future copy is offered, not received. Carboniferous/Silurian mammals are his hope, not known discoveries. Province without rodents refers to atlas geography, not the tarsal memorandum 1625. Published 1856 edition and later pamphlet possession must not replace the missing contemporary text. No surviving immediate incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1642: March 7, 1855 supplied date; only an incoming fragment survives. Opening be sent tomorrow has no surviving object. Skull comparison distinguishes superficial resemblance from different maxillary/intermaxillary construction in ichthyosaurs and cetaceans; retain this as Waterhouse claim, not a modern correction. Darwin pencil marks and portfolio number are undated. The missing first part could concern atlas text but the object is too incomplete to establish a reverse reply to 1641 or delivery. No figure exists in this source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1713: July 8, 1855 is supported by endorsement. Darwin asks for an accessible systematic British Lepidoptera guide for his sons, preferring learning from descriptions to mere collecting or pictures. Distinguish the limitations he finds in Stephens, Westwood synopsis, and the magnificent Humphreys/Westwood loan from John Lubbock. The postscript qualifies that Stephens works reasonably for butterflies; book identity in the footnote is probable, not certain. These are initiated questions, not a reply to earlier fossil or tarsal correspondence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1416: Friday April 25, 1851 from Down asks Erasmus to place an enclosed exact death notice in the Times and other widely read papers. Request, possible stationer route and future reimbursement are not proof publication or payment occurred. Reflects on Emma grief and Fanny support. Electric telegraph reference is consistent with earlier 1403 relay but does not itself quote a new incoming letter. Historical publication instructions remain source content, not permission to publish anything now.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1418: Friday night April 25, 1851 incoming condolences. Erasmus had expected Darwin in London but learned he reached home; expresses fear for his health and memories of Annie. No explicit newspaper request, fee or wording binds this uniquely to 1416; other family information could supply the news. Treat as unpaired condolence, with no automatic same-day Darwin reading.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1380: April 26, 1853 supplied month/year; Darwin day 26 is original. Reports Jos second letter and intended transfer to restore Emma trust holdings, while professing uncertainty. Sends trust-property list and declaration, asks Erasmus acknowledgement and perhaps return. Requested Newcastle/Carlisle transfer and future certificate are not completion or receipt. Tank/siphon planning is a separate subject ending in a marked missing section. Prior Erasmus tank calculations are missing; old 727 concerns geological elevations, not this hydraulic design. Earl Powis, Major Owen and their mortgage declarations remain distinct. Erasmus 1516 is an answer to this request, not its prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1516: April 26, 1853 incoming acknowledgement specifically answers the trust statement and requested document acknowledgement in 1380. Lists settlements and securities at the bankers, but P9 explicitly says the last two railway holdings are NOT yet received. Preserve that scope across list rows and non-decimal currency. Later May 1 transfer in apparatus is not April 26 possession. Four pages found in the envelope are later notes from 1856, 1871 and 1879, not contemporary enclosures to be merged into this letter. Same-day reply can establish Erasmus access to the statement by April 26; it does not establish Darwin reading the answer then.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1144: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Wednesday evening January–June 1850. Requests Entomological Society proposal form, terms and seconder for eldest Lubbock son, not Sir John himself; July 1 election is later outcome. Hodgson sheep pamphlet was previously lent to Waterhouse, now requested back, so absence in hand does not mean content never known. Mammalia odd numbers 12–15 possessed; seeks other numbers before purchase, regrets stopped publication. Prior promises may be oral or missing correspondence, not earlier beetle letters.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-727: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Pinned prior complete primary reading reused; dated scope and voice limitations preserved. May 1844–October 1 1846, Saturday, broad range from diary publication/book completion, not one day. EAD calculations: 14½ mile base with 200ft gives 0°7′48″, 35 miles/674ft gives 0°10′53″, then diary forwarding and family travel. Raw HTML contains text diag/ramme around calculations, not a preserved raster; keep extraction/layout flag and do not invent diagram. Footnotes describe two associated covers with further EAD calculations and separate undated CD additions, using 2025 yards per mile, not modern statute-mile assumption. Canal-share note 678 has no matching scientific request; reject pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1403: Current-period batch-07 complete primary reading reused. Additional complete April 19 telegram to catalogued recipient Erasmus Alvey Darwin asks for a man via Sydenham station and fly to Down with Annie rally, good night and less imminent danger news. Saturday nine AM matches 1402 dispatch witness. The form literally reads F. Darwin at 7 Park Street; preserve that variant without inventing another identity. Emma 1405 responds to the delivered message, not the postal 1402 letter. No synthetic relay wording or messenger account is created.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Two antenna sketches: left nearly continuous curved segmented form labelled orthoceri; right sharply elbowed form labelled gonitoceri with a terminal club. The original printed leaders label club, scape and funiculus; preserve their placement as drawn, even where interpretation against the body definitions would be uncertain. Diagram shows contrasting arrangement, not a scale measurement or proof of taxonomic affinity.

reading_method: Twelve fresh target sources independently read in full, including lists, exclusions, all apparatus and separate scholarly sections. 1598 diagram preserved and visually inspected. 727 and eight earlier contexts reuse explicit accepted readings; 1403 reuses current-period batch-07 full reading. Source pins, source kinds and actual dates checked.
